title: Cascade Analytics - Health, Economics & Roadmap Sprint Planning
summary: Monthly health/usage sync focused on tail latency outliers, cost per inference optimizations, and roadmap alignment for next quarter. Agreed to run a short benchmark comparing current hosted model variant vs a quantized dedicated instance for high-throughput endpoints. Action: share latency percentiles, enable structured traces for two routes, and follow up with pricing scenarios for a Reserved Dedicated pilot.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we've got about 55 minutes, just a couple of goals, s-sprint planning for the next q, quick health check, and some ops items. Diego and Lina are here with me.
[00:12] Priya Nair: Hi hi, thanks Maya, we have Evelyn and Samir, Noah, and Aria on. Agenda looks good, excited to dig in.
[00:22] Lina Park: quick note, I uploaded the incident timeline deck to the shared folder, link in chat.
[00:30] Samir Patel: saw that, thanks. Quick pump — since last call we've had two brief throttles on the /generate-chat route during peak batch windows.
[00:40] Diego Ortiz: yep, we saw the same traces — 503s due to queue exhaustion when batching spiked, we traced to preforking delays on the dedicated workers.
[00:51] Noah Reeves: to add, the KV cache eviction pattern was a bit noisy — we had a few cold starts for high-turnover sessions which hit p99 hard.
[01:02] Maya Chen: ok thanks, useful. For numbers, Priya, can you confirm the rough p95 and p99 you're seeing?
[01:08] Priya Nair: p95 around 180ms, p99 has been jumping between 820 and 1.2s during the busiest hours. It's maybe 0.9s average for the spikes. There's definitely tail.
[01:20] Evelyn Zhao: that's been the customer-facing issue — conversion drops when bot replies lag. We're trying to hold under 300ms on typical queries.
[01:29] Maya Chen: understood. Two levers we recommended: smarter routing (send latency-sensitive small prompts to lower-latency hosted variants) and a dedicated quantized pool for high-throughput long-context jobs.
[01:41] Priya Nair: can you remind us what's the accuracy tradeoff on the quantized variants? We care about hallucination rates.
[01:48] Diego Ortiz: Sure, so int8 quantization yields about 1-2% change on our comparative evals for open models depending on prompt style; for instruction-tuned stacks it's typically negligible, but we'll attach the eval results. There's also mixed-precision paths that keep the attention core in fp16 for critical tokens.
[02:04] Samir Patel: that sounds reasonable, but we need to see regression tests. Do you have a quick bench plan?
[02:10] Lina Park: yes — proposed bench: 24 hour A/B run, 10k requests per endpoint, capture p50/p95/p99, token cost, and quality crawls against our 200-item prompt set. We'll include automated eval diffs.
[02:24] Priya Nair: that would be perfect. Timeline?
[02:27] Maya Chen: we can kickoff a pilot next week subject to approvals — Aria, you mentioned procurement gating?
[02:33] Aria Gomez: procurement needs a short SOW and pricing scenarios. If you can give three options (hosted scale up, dedicated reserved for 3 months, dedicated reserved annual), we can fast-track. Also need SOC2 docs and KMS attestation.
[02:47] Maya Chen: we'll send the SOW + price bands. We have SOC 2 Type II and KMS integration docs — Lina will drop the link.
[02:55] Evelyn Zhao: wanted to call out cost — last month cost spiked due to long-context chats, our token accounting is messy. Samir, any insight?
[03:02] Samir Patel: yea, we had a few workflows that didn't chunk input correctly, so we were sending entire conversation contexts as single requests, and that drove tokens up and caused batching inefficiencies. We're patching the client.
[03:14] Priya Nair: for cost forecasting, we'd like to see per-route token burn and per-token latency cost so we can map to product metrics (CPA).
[03:23] Maya Chen: we can provide token-level breakdown: p50, p95 latency per 1000 tokens and cost per 1k tokens by model variant. We'll include historical 30/90 day.
[03:33] Noah Reeves: plus, can you enable structured traces for the two main routes? The trace IDs will help correlate infra logs.
[03:39] Diego Ortiz: yes we can turn on structured traces for /generate-chat and /embed-batch — low overhead but useful. We'll also include sampling of full KV states for debugging.
[03:50] Priya Nair: on routing, how easy is it to implement rule-based routing in your console? E.g., short prompts to hosted low-latency variants and long to dedicated.
[03:59] Maya Chen: it's built-in — you can set policies by token count, region, or latency SLO. We can propose a default policy and test it in canary for a subset of traffic.
[04:10] Evelyn Zhao: ok that could smooth the p99 tail.
[04:15] Maya Chen: security check: do you need private deployments or is VPC sufficient?
[04:20] Priya Nair: VPC + customer-managed KMS is required for now. On-prem isn't necessary. We may need an airgap option later, but not immediate.
[04:29] Maya Chen: noted. Our Private offering supports VPC + KMS and keeps audit logs. I'll have Lina attach the compliance pack.
[04:36] Aria Gomez: also, can you include data retention settings — we need 7-year audit log retention for compliance.
[04:42] Lina Park: yes, audit retention is configurable; default is 90 days, enterprise add-on supports longer retention, including S3 export.
[04:50] Samir Patel: two quick technical asks: 1) can you provide per-instance GPU utilization metrics per model variant? 2) do you have suggestions for batch sizing to hit 95% utilization without hurting latency?
[05:01] Diego Ortiz: 1) yes, we'll share the GPU utilization dashboards; 2) recommended strategy: continuous batching with adaptive latency windows — we recommend starting with 8-16 token windows for short prompts and 32-64 for long contexts, plus prefix caching for repeated system prompts. We'll send concrete profiles.
[05:21] Priya Nair: for the pilot, what would success metrics look like?
[05:25] Maya Chen: success: p99 reduced below 600ms on the targeted endpoints, cost per 1k tokens down 15% vs hosted baseline, and no measurable regression in our automated quality eval (<=1% drop).
[05:36] Evelyn Zhao: agreed. Also need a 30-day run with weekly checkpoints.
[05:40] Maya Chen: sounds good. Action items coming.
[05:43] Aria Gomez: procurement timeline — once SOW and pricing are in, we can turn in 5 business days.
[05:49] Priya Nair: one more question — what about fallback policies if dedicated pool is saturated?
[05:54] Diego Ortiz: automatic fallback to a compatible hosted variant with a cost/latency knob. You can set strict SLO or best-effort modes. We'll propose a fallback policy that preserves correctness while capping cost.
[06:07] Samir Patel: thanks, that's helpful.
[06:10] Maya Chen: recap: Lina will share SOC2/KMS/compliance pack and incident deck; Diego will enable structured traces and share GPU dashboards; Maya will send SOW and three pricing scenarios; Priya will provide the 200-prompt eval set and confirm the two routes for traces; Aria will share procurement timeline.
[06:29] Lina Park: putting links in the chat now: incident deck, compliance pack, and a bench plan doc.
[06:33] Priya Nair: thanks, I'll drop calendar invites for weekly checkpoints during the 30-day pilot.
[06:39] Evelyn Zhao: ok thanks all, appreciate the responsiveness.
[06:42] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up by email with next steps and proposed pilot start date. Bye.

Notes: transcription contains occasional mislabels and minor noise; timestamps are approximate. Links referenced: /shared/cascade/incident-deck, /shared/cascade/compliance-pack, /shared/cascade/bench-plan
